metadata.description: Fails the run naming every line of a Rust file under engine/crates, outside bnto-core, that splits a name on its last dot itself. A dot in a folder (v1.2/data) or a dotfile (dir/.env) then reads as an extension; use bnto_core::split_extension, file_stem or file_extension (ISS-33). Run it from the repo root.

parameters.script:
# extension-splits: fail naming every line of an engine Rust file, outside
# bnto-core, that splits a name on its last dot with rfind, rsplit_once or
# rsplit. A dot in a folder (v1.2/data) or a dotfile (dir/.env) then reads as
# an extension (ISS-33): use bnto_core::split_extension, file_stem or
# file_extension. bnto/src/output_names.rs splits on its own on purpose: its
# names can hold `\` as well as `/`. Each argument is one file, relative to
# engine/crates.
# Gap: a content-search node will replace this step (dogfooding.md, PR 9).
cd engine/crates || exit 2
files=""
for f in "$@"; do
  case $f in
    bnto-core/*|bnto/src/output_names.rs) ;;
    *) files="$files $f" ;;
  esac
done
# The dot between the quotes is matched by `.`: the pattern can't hold a `'`.
found=$(grep -HnE '[.]r(find|split_once|split)[(].[.].[)]' -- $files)
case $? in
  0) ;;
  1) echo "No engine Rust file outside bnto-core splits a name on its last dot."; exit 0 ;;
  *) exit 2 ;;
esac
echo "Names split on their last dot (use bnto_core::split_extension; see ISS-33):" >&2
printf '%s\n' "$found" | sed 's|^|  engine/crates/|' >&2
exit 1
